title: Timeline template
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Biographies: conviction, justice and legacy
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 62 (Timeline template (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 62: Biography: Muhammad Ali's life and the features of a biography. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Features of a biography
points: The writer's view of the person's legacy

timeline.text: Born Cassius Clay in Louisville, Kentucky
Begins boxing aged 12, after his bicycle is stolen
World heavyweight champion; becomes Muslim and takes the name Muhammad Ali

timeline.label: 1967 to 1971
timeline.text: Refuses the military draft on religious grounds; banned; the Supreme Court overturns his conviction

timeline.label: 1974 to 2016
timeline.text: Regains the title; later humanitarian work; dies in 2016

model.title: What is your first impression of Ali's character?

parts.text: Point: Ali was determined from a young age
Evidence: he began boxing at 12 after his bicycle was stolen
Explain: he turned anger into a goal
Link: this determination runs through his whole life

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Ali seems determined: when his bicycle was stolen at 12, he turned his anger into training, a quality that shaped his career.

keywords.def: the story of a real person's life, written by someone else
a firmly held belief that guides your actions

questions.q: When and where did Ali win Olympic gold?
Why was Ali banned from boxing in 1967?
questions.a: he refused the military draft because of his religious beliefs

questions.q: Core: complete the timeline with eight events and write two sentences on why each of two events matters
Extend: in the Biography Journal, record five significant events and five new words
questions.a: Five events and five words with definitions

questions.q: Stretch: explain the difference between a biography and an autobiography, with an example of each feature
questions.a: Third person vs first person; written by others vs by the subject

questions.q: Ali lost three and a half years of his career rather than go against his beliefs. What does this show?
questions.a: B) conviction. Giving up so much for a belief shows conviction: a firmly held principle guiding his actions.

questions.q: A biography is usually written in...
One word for Ali's character, with a reason
questions.a: For example: principled, because he gave up his title for his beliefs
